# Best RV power station and solar panel combo

**My pick for most RVers: BLUETTI AC200L + ALLPOWERS SP037 400W folding panel, about $1,123 with codes.**

- **[BLUETTI AC200L](https://dealectric.com/go/bluetti-ac200l)**: $899, or $854.05 with code AFF5OFF. It has 2,048Wh of LiFePO4 capacity, 2,400W output, and a built-in TT-30 (30A) RV outlet. It accepts up to 1,200W of solar and expands to 8,192Wh. It weighs about 28 kg (62 lb) ([Dealectric](https://dealectric.com/answers/best-rv-portable-power-station-solar-panel-combo-2026-comparison-ecoflow-bluetti)).
- **[ALLPOWERS SP037 400W panel](https://dealectric.com/go/allpowers-sp037-400w-solar-panel)**: $299, or $269.10 with code ALLPOWER26. It is IP67-rated, and its voltage is compatible with the AC200L's solar input.

**Caveats:**
- The two items come from different stores, so you'll check out twice.
- The panel is heavy for a folding model (18.5 kg).
- Dealectric is an affiliate site, and it only compared BLUETTI and ALLPOWERS. Its prices and codes were tested on Oct 21, 2026 and may change.
- A 13,500 BTU roof AC draws about 1,500W running but spikes past 3,000W at startup ([EmergencyEnergy](https://www.emergencyenergy.co/articles/rv-power-station/)). The AC200L's 3,600W surge rating is close to that, so you may want a soft-start kit if you plan to run the AC.

## Alternatives

- **More capacity, stays in the RV:** [ALLPOWERS R4000](https://dealectric.com/go/allpowers-r4000-3456wh) has 3,456Wh, 3,600W output, an RV outlet, and 2,000W of solar input. With one SP037 the pair is about $1,588. It weighs 45 kg, so it's not hand-carry.
- **Full-time boondocking or running AC:** The EcoFlow DELTA Pro 3 (4,096Wh, 4,000W, expandable past 12kWh) is the top pick in [EmergencyEnergy's RV comparison](https://www.emergencyenergy.co/articles/rv-power-station/). It's heavy and the priciest option, and those results list no price. The Jackery Explorer 3000 Pro (3,000W, 3,024Wh) is a simpler option for AC loads. I don't have direct buy links for these from my results.
- **Weekend trips, light and simple:** The Jackery Explorer 1000 v2 (1,070Wh, 23.8 lb) pairs with SolarSaga panels. Its solar input caps at 400W, and it isn't expandable ([Smart Energy Edge](https://smartenergyedge.com/best-portable-power-station-with-solar-panels-for-camping/)).

## Sizing tip
Add up your watts times hours. A 150W fridge over 10 hours is about 1,500Wh ([Acquired Sense](https://www.acquiredsense.com/reviews/power-stations.html)). For a 2,000Wh unit, a 300–400W folding array can refill it in a full day of decent sun.

If you tell me whether you'll run the roof AC, how many nights you boondock, and your budget, I can narrow this down.
